chapters.title: morning light
chapters.html:
This isn’t what he thought of, at first. 

He plans on waking up early, when dawn barely breaks on the horizon and the darkness of their bedroom is slowly unveiled. He wants to witness— enjoy the sight of his sleeping husband’s face gradually being touched by the morning light, softly glowing like the sun and the emissaries of enlightenment he believes Mydei is. He wants to take his time staring at his husband’s beauty, so manly and so beautiful at the same time, before shielding him from the light with their bed’s curtain to ensure that his slumber remains undisturbed. They were awake until late at night due to their consummation and while he acknowledges that Mydei has stamina and vigor like no other, properly rested Mydei is still the best Mydei in his opinion.

After carefully slipping out of their bed, he plans to make something for both of them. Preferably something that smells delicious and appetizing, so that it will rouse the younger man up and he can look more dependable and husband-able (Castorice’s word, not his) in front of Mydei. Even if Mydei is still asleep by the time he finishes cooking their breakfast, he doesn’t mind the scenario where he wakes the beige-red-haired man up. Gently calling Mydei’s name and being the first thing Mydei sees as soon as he's awake— it’s truly not a bad option. 

He already has everything prepared in his mind, but…

“You’re awake.” 

Phainon softly exhales in defeat, as he leans against the wall and stares at the situation across from him. Clad in a black apron, Mydei is already awake and alert, casually and skillfully handling several pots and pans on the stove. The delicious scent of garlic, herbs, and seared meat fills the air, mingling with a robust and savory aroma of coffee.

He shakes his head, licking his lips before standing straight and approaching the other man. 

“You beat me to it.” Phainon chuckles, a sincere smile tugs on his lips despite his plans going awry. “I was going to get up early and cook you something for our first morning together.” He shrugs. 

“I did wear you out last night.” Mydei responds breezily and the implication tickles Phainon into another chuckle. 

“Wasn’t it the other way around?” Phainon teases back as he finally stops right behind Mydei. Wrapping his arms around the other’s waist, he leans his face forward to steal a kiss on the younger male’s cheek. “I remember someone begging me to stop moving for a moment last night.” 

“Which you first ignored, HKS.” Mydei dryly reminds, stirring a whitish, thick-looking soup on his left. 

“I’m sorry, I was too preoccupied with the face you made to hear it the first time around.” Phainon shamelessly admits as he gives an apologetic kiss on Mydei’s hickey-littered neck. “You clawed my arms in return, so can we think of it as even?” 

“You wish.” Mydei scoffs.

“Well, I can always compensate you. I don’t mind you riding and using me as you please this morning—” 

“Get your mind out of the gutter, you damn HKS.” Mydei lightly scolds. “We have some itineraries this morning until afternoon.” 

“We are newlyweds.” Phainon counters, a little bit whining. “Surely anyone can understand if we are to disappear from society for, I don’t know, a month?” 

“That’d be the case, but we have duties to tend to before that.” Mydei replies as he turns off the stove. “We have to make at least one formal appearance to the public before we leave for our honeymoon. Lady Aglaea and Lady Tribios have kindly entertained our guests in our stead, so it’s only right that we greet them this morning as well.”

“Right.” Phainon sighs as he lets go of his hold. “I completely forgot about that.”

“You only prioritized the wedding night huh, HKS?” 

“You made me sound like a pervert.” Phainon scrunches his face in displeasure and a bark of laughter escapes from Mydei at the sight. 

“And you complain that Lady Tribios still calls you ‘Phai-chan’. I find it quite befitting of the way you act behind closed doors.” Mydei remarks amusedly.

“How rude, Dei.” Phainon huffs before something connects in his mind. “Is that why you cook so much? You want to bring some for them?” He questions as he looks around. 

“These are for us.” Mydei rebukes. “The ones for Lady Aglaea and Lady Tribios are already in the fridge. I made some light desserts for them.” 

“You’re so amazing, Dei.” Phainon unconsciously murmurs as Mydei starts to walk around and put the pots and pans onto the kitchen’s island.

“In contrast, you’re so easy to please, Deliverer.” Mydei smirks. “Besides, it’s customary in Castrum Kremnos for newlyweds to greet each other’s parents on the morning of their wedding.” He continues evenly as he pours the soup into a big bowl. “Mainly to ensure that the bride doesn’t murder their groom and vice versa, but the tradition sticks regardless.”

“I really don’t mind being murdered if it’s by you.”

“How embarrassing, Deliverer.” The younger man muses.

“I said what I said.” Phainon shrugs. “Oh now that I think about it, Krateros mentioned it last night.” 

“He did?” Mydei raises his eyebrow.

“Yeah and…” Phainon continues more carefully. “Are you sure you’re alright with this, Dei?” 

“What are you speaking of now?” Mydei inquires with a frown. 

“Well…” Phainon scratches the back of his head. “I heard from him that Kremnoans celebrate their wedding for three days and three nights, even more for one of noble blood, but you never said anything so I wonder—”

“Phainon of Okhema, formerly of Aedes Elysiae.”

Upon hearing the steel-like tone, Phainon automatically stands straight, knowing that he’s in a little trouble. “Yes?” 

“Come here.” Mydei beckons to him.

There is only a few meters gap between them, but…

“How about no?” He bargains with his most convincing, charming smile.

“Phainon.” 

His body immediately moves as his husband’s wish, stopping right across the unamused Castrum Kremnos’ last royalty. 

“I understand that you brought this up out of goodwill, but if you dare to continue that sentence, you’ll insult me like no other.” Mydei solemnly says. 

Phainon churns up a more apologetic smile as he casts his gaze down accordingly. “I’m sorry. It wasn’t my— Ouch—!”

A sharp sting explodes at the center of his forehead and Phainon instinctively clutches his head at the pain, instantly looking up at the other. 

“I know what I want and how I want it.” Mydei retreats his right hand before crossing his arms on his chest. “Defying some useless and wasteful tradition isn’t new to me, HKS.” 

“It isn’t my intention to offend you.” Phainon murmurs. 

“Did I say otherwise?” Mydei points out with a look as he stretches his hand and gently rubs the reddening area where he flicked with his fingers.

“I just… We did hasten our wedding impulsively and it only occurred to me last night that mayhaps you have some traditions you’d want to—” 

“Again, continue that sentence and I have no qualm about physically beating some sense into you, Phainon.” Mydei remarks evenly. 

“Zipped.” Phainon motions with his fingers.

The beige-red-haired male exhales deeply. “Is this what momentarily bothered you last night?”

“Well, yes.” Phainon admits honestly. “Though I forgot about it when you… well…” He continues with a guilty grin. “To be fair, you were truly distracting and utterly divine, Dei.” 

Mydei lets out an almost exasperated, though no less fond, soft scoff. “Let’s reverse the question then, Deliverer. How about you?” He says with a wave of his hand. 

“Me?” 

“As Lady Aglaea’s chosen heir, you are bound to have greater things—” 

“No.” Phainon swiftly catches the other’s wrist and grips it tightly. “If it isn’t you, then it has no meaning.” 

“Right…” 

“I speak the truth.” Phainon shakes his head. The hand that’s gripping Mydei’s wrist moves forward to intertwine their hand, while his other free hand tucks Mydei’s free hair to the back of his ear. “There is only one person I am willing to share my life with, and he is currently standing right in front of me.” 

“Such cheesiness delivered with a straight face, Deliverer.” Mydei teases with a smirk. “Though I suppose that’s part of your charm.”

“One that is only reserved for you.” Phainon adds with a more relaxed and sincere smile. “Besides, objectively speaking, it is you who marries beneath your station. I am not originally a royalty by blood.” 

“Oh I don’t know, having a handsome puppy-like husband who can keep me on my toes sounds wonderful than some snobby, incompetent one.” Mydei muses.

“Indeed.” Phainon nods agreeingly. “I am the only one worthy to be by your side.” 

“Then there is no more to be discussed about.” Mydei says firmly. “Additionally, it’ll be prudent of you to disregard most of what Krateros says. You shall listen to me and none other, understood?”

Phainon nods as he pulls his husband’s hand close and kisses his knuckle. “As you wish.”

Mydei lets out another scoff. “Knock off your antics, Prince Charming.” He says as he pulls his hand back. “Now that we have cleared it up, go make yourself useful and get us some plates.” 

“So bossy.” Phainon teases. Instead of moving to do what he’s tasked, Phainon shamelessly moves to embrace the other male into his hold and rest his chin on his shoulder. “I haven’t even gotten my morning kiss, Dei.” 

“Get off of me, Deliverer.” 

“Nope.” Phainon replies cheerfully. “Not before I get my kiss.” 

The Kremnoan sighs. “You weren’t this spoiled when we were dating.” 

“Because I thought you won’t like it.” Phainon hums.

“But it doesn’t matter now?” Mydei guesses dryly. 

“Correct, because I’m officially, legally your husband now.” Phainon chirps unabashedly. “No take back, no refund. It’s a one-time sale and purchase.”

“Well, one-time sale and purchase Prince Charming, I’d like to have our meal when they’re still hot and if I remember correctly, Lady Cipher hinted at giving us a mischievous gift fitting for a newlywed. The sooner we do our duties, the sooner we can return here—” 

“On it— Let me get those plates and let us depart as soon as possible, Dei!”
